Question: What makes a good leader according to the Bible?
ShortAnswer: A good leader, in the Bible's picture, is a servant: someone of proven character who leads by example, puts others' good first, and follows Jesus, the Good Shepherd. Biblical leadership is measured by service, not by power.
DetailedAnswer: Jesus redefined leadership completely: 'Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant' (Mark 10:42-45). The world's leaders use power for themselves; Jesus' leaders use it for others, following His own example of giving His life as a ransom. Paul's qualifications for church leaders focus on character, not charisma: above reproach, self-controlled, hospitable, able to teach, not a lover of money (1 Timothy 3:1-7; Titus 1:7-9). The Old Testament adds the same pattern: Moses learned to share leadership rather than carry it alone (Exodus 18:21), Nehemiah refused to exploit his people even when he had the right to (Nehemiah 5:14-19), and David, for all his failures, was a man after God's own heart. Good leaders also tell the truth, admit mistakes, protect the vulnerable, and develop others rather than hoarding influence. The test is simple: does this leader look like the Good Shepherd, who lays down His life for the sheep (John 10:11) — or like a hired hand, who runs when trouble comes? Follow the shepherds; be one.
BibleReferences: Mark 10:42-45; 1 Timothy 3:1-7; Titus 1:7-9; Nehemiah 5:14-19; Exodus 18:21; John 10:11
